headline: Home Depot's US comps rose just 0.4% as fewer transactions and muted big projects offset higher tickets; outlook reaffirmed.
guidance_note: Reaffirmed FY2026: total sales +2.5-4.5%, comps ~flat to +2%, adj EPS ~flat to +4%; flagged rate, tariff and energy-price volatility.
key_messages: US comps +0.4% (total +0.6%, incl. ~55bps FX): ticket +2.2%, comparable transactions -1.3%.
Big-ticket (>$1,000) comparable transactions +0.8%; large cross-category projects remain muted.
Adj EPS $3.43 vs $3.56 a year earlier; sales +4.8% driven mostly by GMS.
Decker: underlying demand similar to FY2025 despite greater consumer uncertainty and housing affordability pressure.
Online sales +10.5%; Pro growth and spring categories (record Q1 in power) supported results.

consumer.big_ticket: Big-ticket transactions +0.8%, but uncertainty is holding customers back from large projects while housing turnover stays low.
consumer.pricing: Ticket gains reflect mix and modest price increases; management cited tariffs, energy prices and interest rates as sources of volatility.

macro_read: Flat-ish real demand: households keep up maintenance but defer big projects given elevated mortgage rates, low turnover and fuel costs weighing on confidence.

sources.label: Nasdaq: Home Depot Q1 earnings call highlights
